title: Dadiji’s First Day with Saarthi
paragraphs: Meet Savitri, or as everyone in her society calls her, Dadiji. At 68, she has more friends than her son does, more blessings than worries, and one steady routine - her morning visit to the mandir.

Her son had grown concerned about her tiring temple trips. One afternoon he sat beside her and introduced her to Saarthi, a service that helps seniors have a safer, easier and more peaceful mandir experience. He explained that family members could also use it on their behalf, and since many seniors prefer WhatsApp over new apps, Saarthi also works entirely through WhatsApp. Dadiji liked that she wouldn’t have to learn anything new. That evening, she received her first welcome message. It asked a few simple questions about the temple she visits, the days she prefers and her usual timings. She replied happily, surprised at how simple it felt.

The next morning, while having chai, she received her daily update. It showed the aarti timing, crowd level and estimated wait. She typed that she wanted to go at ten. Saarthi then suggested, “Ms. Kulkarni from your area is planning a 12 PM visit. Would you like to share a ride?” Dadiji smiled but declined today. A moment later, it asked if she needed a ride booking. She said yes and soon received her cab details, along with an audio story for her journey, and primary volunteer details. At the temple gate, she saw the Darshan Forecast Board and felt relieved. She spotted Rohit who was wearing the Saarthi t-shirt. He greeted her, checked her Saarthi pass, took her slippers and handed her, her offering token. Along the route, Saarthi volunteers stood at calm checkpoints with shade, seating and water. At the top-most checkpoint, a volunteer matched her token to her pre-booked thali and handed it to her gently.

After a peaceful darshan, she accepted a take-home prasad kit and sat at the exit rest station, where her slippers were returned. At the exit she notices a Saarthi ambulance standing nearby, reassuring her that help was close if needed. She went home, by the cab that was already waiting for her. On the way back she was smiling, feeling cared for from start to finish.
